sections.h2: Which Harnett County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
The Harnett County Tax Department, based in Lillington, lists, appraises and bills every parcel in the county, and its Collection Division takes the payments. Real property valuation questions go to the Real Property Division at 910-814-6920, while bill and payment questions go to 910-893-7520 or taxinfo@harnett.org.

Collections are at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington, NC 27546. The register of deeds uses the same street address at Suite 200, which is handy when a sale needs both a payoff figure and a recorded deed.

Real property is listed automatically every year, so owners do not receive an annual listing form. The county does ask owners to report new structures and additions, and its appraisers work from building permits issued by the county or a municipal permit office.

sections.h2: When are Harnett County property taxes due, and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Harnett County property tax is due September 1 and counts as on time through January 5 of the next year. Interest of 2% starts January 6, followed by three-quarters of one percent for each month after that, which tracks G.S. 105-360.

The Tax Department mailed the 2026 bills on August 28, 2026 and set January 5, 2027 as the last day before delinquency. Owners can pay in equal monthly amounts or in any amount they choose while the bill is open, and each payment is applied to the bill with an updated statement mailed back.

sections.h2: What are the payment options and fees in Harnett County?
sections.html:
Owners can pay online, by phone at 1-866-580-9996, by mail, or in person, and cash is taken only at the Tax Department itself. Checks, certified checks and money orders work in person or by mail.

  • Personal debit cards carry a $3.80 convenience fee per transaction.
  • Credit cards carry 2.50% of the balance owing.
  • Business credit or debit cards on high-rewards programs carry 3.25%.
  • E-checks carry $2.00 per transaction.

Those fees go to the payment processor, not to the county. A returned check voids the payment, and the county adds the greater of 10% of the check or $25.00 to the bill. Once a bill is delinquent the office does not make payment arrangements, so anyone planning to pay in installments should start before January 6.

sections.h2: How does Harnett County value a house?
sections.html:
The Real Property Division values all real property at fair market value using a computer-assisted mass appraisal system, and the county reports more than 73,000 parcels. It looks at site inspections, zoning and soil classes, deeds, market sales and aerial photography.

The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2022. On the advice of the state Department of Revenue, the commissioners then moved the county to a four-year cycle, which put the next reappraisal at January 1, 2026. State law sets the outer limit at eight years under G.S. 105-286.

A structure is valued by its percent complete on January 1. A garage finished in March therefore adds nothing to that year's bill. That timing matters for a seller who has just built or renovated, because the value on the bill may lag the real condition of the house.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Harnett County property value?
sections.html:
Start by asking the Real Property Division how it takes value reviews after the 2026 reappraisal, then use the county board of equalization and review if the answer does not settle it. The board is the board of commissioners unless a special board exists, and under G.S. 105-322 its first meeting falls no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May.

  • Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment.
  • A further appeal to the Property Tax Commission is filed within 30 days after the board mailed its notice.

Bring sales of similar nearby houses, repair estimates and photos. A value tied to January 1 of the reappraisal year is easier to contest with evidence from that date.

sections.h2: Which relief programs apply to Harnett County homeowners?
sections.html:
Harnett County sends owners to its exemptions page and to a present-use value program for farm and forest land. Three state programs for permanent residences run through the county assessor on Form AV-9, and an owner can draw on only one.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4.0% of income at or under the limit and 5.0% above it up to $58,200, with unpaid amounts deferred as a lien.

Applications should be filed in the listing period but are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. Deferred taxes for the preceding three fiscal years come due on a transfer, so a seller on the circuit-breaker program should expect that balance at closing.

sections.h2: What happens when Harnett County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax is advertised each spring, and the 2025 liens ran in The Daily Record on May 12, 2026. The county names the owner as of January 6 and adds an advertising fee to the bill.

Harnett mostly uses the mortgage-style foreclosure method, a civil action ending in a courthouse-steps auction by a court-appointed commissioner. The county page calls for a 10% deposit at the sale, then a 10-day upset bid window, and each upset bid must top the last by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The owner can redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, fees and costs.

The county also says North Carolina sells no tax lien certificates, so a third party who pays a delinquent bill does not gain title. Before collection reaches foreclosure, the office tries bank attachment, wage garnishment, rent attachment and sheriff levy.

sections.h2: What should I know about property tax when selling in Harnett County?
sections.html:
A seller owes the tax on the parcel through closing, and the payoff comes out of the sale proceeds. Ask the Collection Division for a written balance, including interest and any advertising fee, before the closing date is set.

The deed excise tax is separate. The transferor pays it to the register of deeds before recording, at $1.00 per $500 of value, so it appears as a seller cost on the settlement statement. A house with delinquent tax, a foreclosure filing or a deferred circuit-breaker balance can still sell, but the lender and tax office need to be paid in the right order.

County numbers help set expectations for pricing and timing:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 150,137, up 12.4% from the 2020 base.
  • Housing units: 59,085, with 71.0% owner-occupied.
  • Median owner-occupied home value for 2020-2024: $246,200.
  • Median household income: $71,287, and mean travel time to work is 32.8 minutes.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2,205 (Census QuickFacts).

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Harnett County property tax early?
faqs.a: No. The county page states that Harnett County offers no discount on ad valorem property tax. Owners can make prepayments from February through August, which spreads the cost but earns no reduction.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Harnett County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: January 5 of the year after the bill is issued. For the 2026 bills that day is January 5, 2027, and interest begins on January 6.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Harnett County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and any advertising fee are paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the Collection Division for a current payoff first. If a foreclosure case has been filed, the balance also includes court costs and attorney fees.

faqs.q: Does Harnett County reappraise property every year?
faqs.a: No. The county moved to a four-year cycle after its January 1, 2022 reappraisal, and its next scheduled reappraisal is January 1, 2026. Between reappraisals, values change when a property changes, such as new construction or an addition.

faqs.q: Where do I pay or ask about a Harnett County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay online, by phone at 1-866-580-9996, by mail, or at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington. Questions about a bill go to 910-893-7520 or taxinfo@harnett.org.
